citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
The principal investigator did not conduct sedation and monitoring procedures in accordance with the IACUC approved
protocol (PROTO202300033). The PI used assumed body weights, underdosed atropine, prepared reversal agents using
an undocumented dilution method, and did not document protocol required anesthetic monitoring and recovery
parameters. These deviations occurred across a cohort of infant rhesus macaques born in May–June 2025 and continued
as these same animals reached one year of age, demonstrating repeated departures from the protocol’s described weight
based dosing and required monitoring over time.
Because the protocol must provide “a complete description of the proposed use of the animals” and requires activities to
match that description, these departures represent protocol adherence failures. Such deviations are important because
they reduce the IACUC’s ability to ensure that procedures limit discomfort and safeguard welfare. In this case, deviations
in dosing and monitoring could compromise physiologic stability during sedation, and incomplete monitoring may fail to
detect signs of distress or adverse reactions. Protocols must contain a complete description of the proposed use of the
animals, and activities must be conducted in accordance with that description.
Correct by: September 29, 2026

The facility failed to provide potable water to a rhesus macaque (animal #685) for two consecutive days (February 7–8,
2026) following a cage reconfiguration, as evident during the record review portion of the inspection. The animal did not
receive continuous water nor twice daily watering. Because water deprivation directly affects hydration, organ function,
and stress physiology, a two day lapse can negatively affect the health and well being of the animal. Potable water must
be provided in sufficient quantity to every nonhuman primate, and when continuous access is not provided, water must be
offered at least twice daily to ensure health and well being.
Correct by: September 16, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
